I am 29, I never went to school, and I farm here in Quzhou with my husband and our two young children. We have about 10 mu of land. I cannot read the words on fertilizer bags, but I know farming from watching my mother-in-law and the neighbors, and I know what works on this land.

My wheat is already in the ground from last October — I always plant improved wheat seeds because that is what the shop in town sells and what everyone around me uses. Before planting I rotary-till the soil to break it up, then I put down compound fertilizer as a base. This spring I will irrigate three times and topdress with urea when the wheat starts to joint, and I will spray four times for aphids and weeds. I expect about 500 kg per mu, which gives us enough flour for the year and some grain to sell.

After we harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant maize straight into the wheat stubble without tilling — we have been doing no-tillage for years now because it saves diesel and time, and the maize grows just fine. I buy hybrid maize seeds because they grow fast and strong in the short summer season. I fertilize with compound fertilizer and a little extra nitrogen, irrigate twice when the summer heat comes, and spray three times for borers and weeds. I expect about 550 kg per mu.

I also keep 3 mu for cotton because the cash helps pay for the children’s clothes and school supplies, even though I never went to school myself. Cotton is hard work — I rotary-till that plot, plant improved cotton seeds, and I know I will have to spray sixteen times through the season for bollworms and weeds, and irrigate twice. Picking is done by hand, which takes many days, but the money is reliable. I expect about 275 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I do what the other farmers do. If my neighbors change something and it works, I will try it too. For now, this is my plan.
